OPENCTI_URL.description: The base URL of the OpenCTI instance.

OPENCTI_TOKEN.description: The API token to connect to OpenCTI.

CONNECTOR_SCOPE.description: The entity types this connector ingests into OpenCTI.

CONNECTOR_LOG_LEVEL.description: The minimum level of logs to display.

CONNECTOR_DURATION_PERIOD.description: How long to wait between two ingestion runs.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_COLLECTION_IDS.description: Comma-separated list of Censys collection IDs to ingest. Leave empty to ingest all collections for the organisation. Takes precedence over 'excluded_collection_ids' if both are set.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_EXCLUDED_COLLECTION_I.description: Comma-separated list of Censys collection IDs to exclude from ingestion; every other collection visible to the organisation is ingested. Ignored if 'collection_ids' is set.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_TLP_LEVEL.description: TLP marking applied to all ingested observables and indicators.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_INDICATOR_SCORE.description: Confidence score (0–100) assigned to ingested observables and indicators.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_AUTO_INDICATOR_BY_SCO.description: If enabled (default), an indicator is only auto-created for an observable when its score meets or exceeds 'indicator_score_threshold'. If disabled, an indicator is auto-created for every ingested observable, regardless of score.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_INDICATOR_SCORE_THRES.description: Minimum score (0–100) an observable must have for an indicator to be auto-created. Only used when 'auto_indicator_by_score' is enabled.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_SKIP_UNCHANGED_COLLEC.description: If enabled (default), a collection that has already been ingested is skipped when Censys reports no asset additions since its last successful ingestion. Changes to existing assets (e.g. new vulnerabilities on a host) are only picked up once the collection is ingested again. If disabled, every collection is fully re-ingested on every run.

CENSYS_COLLECTIONS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECON.description: Per-request timeout (in seconds) for calls to the Censys API. Increase this if large collections cause read timeouts.
